turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good morning, Mr. Tan. I'm Dr. Lim, the anesthesiologist who will be taking care of you during your hernia repair surgery. I'd like to go through some questions to make sure we're all set for tomorrow's procedure. Is that okay with you?

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Great. Let's start with your medical history. You've been diagnosed with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and osteoarthritis in your knees. Can you tell me a bit about how these are being managed?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Sure. My blood pressure is under control with losartan. I take metformin for my diabetes, and tamsulosin for my prostate. For my knees, I take diclofenac when the pain gets bad, like after walking too much.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thank you. Now, regarding your medications, I see in your records that you were on aspirin 75 mg daily. Can you confirm if you're still taking that, and if not, when did you stop and why?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Oh, I stopped taking aspirin already. It's been about two years ago. I had some stomach discomfort, like heartburn, so I stopped. I didn't have any issues since then, so I just continued with the other medications.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: I see. That's important to know. Are you currently taking all your regular medications as prescribed, except for the aspirin?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, Doctor. I take losartan every morning, metformin twice a day, and tamsulosin once at night. Diclofenac only when needed.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. Do you have any known allergies to medications or other substances?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, none that I know of.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia? If so, were there any complications?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I had a minor operation on my finger many years ago, and that was under general anesthesia. I don't remember any problems, just a bit of nausea after.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Thanks for sharing that. How about your current physical condition? Are you able to walk independently, climb stairs, and perform daily activities without much difficulty?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Yes, I can walk and climb stairs, but sometimes my knees give me trouble if I overdo it. Otherwise, I'm quite independent.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. Finally, have you had anything to eat or drink since midnight?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, Doctor. I stopped eating after 8 PM last night, as instructed. Just a bit of water with my morning medications.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Perfect. Well, Mr. Tan, that covers most of what I needed to know. We'll be using general anesthesia with a laryngeal mask airway for your surgery. I'll make sure to note your medication changes and allergies in your chart. If you have any more questions, feel free to ask.

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Thank you, Doctor. I think that's all from me for now.
